maryland.label: Maryland
maryland.bookValueRule: If vehicle is 7 years old or newer, MVA may assess on book value; a notarized bill of sale overrides
notes: Title fee increased from $100 to $200 effective July 1, 2025.
Maryland MVA collects a mandatory $40/yr EMS surcharge bundled into registration fees.
Private-party sales are taxed on the full agreed price or book value; trade-in deductions are not permitted by MD statute.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with the Maryland MVA.
Vehicles 7 years old or newer may be assessed on book value, not your purchase price, unless you present a notarized bill of sale.
Maryland taxes the full purchase price — trade-ins and rebates do not reduce excise tax.

faqs.question: Do I pay sales tax on a private car sale in Maryland?
faqs.answer: Yes. In Maryland, private vehicle purchases are subject to a 6.5% vehicle excise tax collected by the Maryland Motor Vehicle Administration (MVA) when you apply for the title certificate. There is a statutory minimum excise tax floor of $41.60 (based on a minimum $640 vehicle valuation).

faqs.question: How much is the Maryland title transfer fee?
faqs.answer: The certificate of title fee in Maryland is $200.00 for both new and used vehicles (increased from $100 on July 1, 2025). If your purchase is financed, an additional $40 security interest (lien) filing fee applies.

faqs.question: How does Maryland calculate vehicle excise tax on private sales?
faqs.answer: For vehicles older than 7 years, the 6.5% excise tax is calculated directly on the purchase price stated on the title. For vehicles 7 years old or newer, the MVA assesses tax on whichever is higher: the purchase price or the NADA clean retail book value, unless the buyer and seller submit a notarized Maryland Bill of Sale (Form VR-181) verifying the lower price.

faqs.question: Does a trade-in reduce vehicle excise tax in Maryland?
faqs.answer: No. Under Maryland law, trade-in deductions are only permitted on purchases from licensed Maryland motor vehicle dealers. In a private-party sale, the excise tax base is the full purchase price; any trade-in value does not reduce your tax obligation.

faqs.question: How much are Maryland vehicle registration and tag fees?
faqs.answer: Maryland offers both 1-year and 2-year registration terms. For Class A passenger vehicles weighing 3,700 lbs or less, registration is $125.50 for 1 year or $251.00 for 2 years (including the mandatory annual $40 EMS surcharge). For vehicles over 3,700 lbs, registration is $191.50 for 1 year or $383.00 for 2 years. Motorcycles are $105.00 for 1 year or $210.00 for 2 years. Zero-emission electric vehicles (ZEVs) have an additional $125/year surcharge, while plug-in hybrids (PHEVs) have a $100/year surcharge.

virginia.label: Virginia
virginia.bookValueRule: Vehicles 5 years old or newer sold below NADA trade-in value may be taxed on NADA value unless a Virginia DMV SUT-1A affidavit is submitted.
notes: Virginia levies a 4.15% Motor Vehicle Sales and Use Tax (SUT) with a $75.00 minimum floor.
Virginia taxes the gross purchase price; trade-ins are not deductible under VA Code § 58.1-2401.
A $2.00 discount applies when registering passenger vehicles or motorcycles for a 2-year term.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with the Virginia DMV.
Virginia taxes the full sales price — trade-ins and rebates do not reduce Motor Vehicle Sales and Use Tax.
Vehicles 5 years old or newer sold below NADA value may be assessed on NADA trade-in value unless form SUT-1A is submitted.

faqs.question: What is the Virginia sales tax on a private car purchase?
faqs.answer: Virginia imposes a 4.15% Motor Vehicle Sales and Use Tax (SUT) based on the gross sales price, with a statutory minimum tax of $75.00.

faqs.question: How much is the title certificate fee in Virginia?
faqs.answer: The Virginia DMV charges $15.00 for an original or transferred certificate of title. If the vehicle is financed, an additional $15.00 supplemental lien filing fee applies.

faqs.question: Does a trade-in reduce sales tax in Virginia?
faqs.answer: No. Under Virginia law (VA Code § 58.1-2401), the Motor Vehicle Sales and Use Tax is calculated on the gross sales price. Trade-in deductions are not permitted on private-party or dealer transactions.

faqs.question: How much are vehicle registration fees in Virginia?
faqs.answer: Virginia passenger vehicle registration is weight-based: $30.75/year for vehicles 4,000 lbs or less ($59.50 for 2 years with the $2 discount) and $35.75/year for vehicles over 4,000 lbs ($69.50 for 2 years). Motorcycles are $24.75/year ($47.50 for 2 years).

pennsylvania.label: Pennsylvania
notes: Pennsylvania sales tax is 6% baseline (7% in Allegheny County, 8% in Philadelphia).
Certificate of title fee is $72.00 pursuant to PennDOT Form MV-70S biennial CPI adjustment (increased from older $58 schedule).
Trade-in deduction is only allowed at licensed Pennsylvania dealerships; private party sales cannot deduct trade-ins.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with PennDOT.
Pennsylvania sales tax is 6% statewide (7% in Allegheny County, 8% in City of Philadelphia).
Private vehicle purchases in Pennsylvania do not qualify for trade-in tax credits; tax is owed on the full agreed purchase price.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate in Pennsylvania?
faqs.answer: The Pennsylvania state sales tax rate on motor vehicles is 6% of the purchase price. Residents of Allegheny County pay 7% (additional 1% local tax) and residents of Philadelphia pay 8% (additional 2% local tax).

faqs.question: How much is the Pennsylvania vehicle title transfer fee?
faqs.answer: The certificate of title fee in Pennsylvania is $72.00 according to PennDOT Form MV-70S. If the vehicle is financed, a $36.00 lien recordation fee is also required.

faqs.question: Does a trade-in reduce sales tax on private sales in Pennsylvania?
faqs.answer: No. Pennsylvania only allows trade-in credits when you trade a vehicle into a licensed dealership. Private-to-private sales are taxed on the full purchase price or market value without trade-in deduction.

faqs.question: How much is vehicle registration in Pennsylvania?
faqs.answer: Standard passenger vehicle registration in Pennsylvania is $48.00 per year ($96.00 for 2 years). Certain counties add an optional $5.00 local use fee. Motorcycle registration is $25.00 per year ($50.00 for 2 years).

delaware.label: Delaware
notes: Delaware has no general sales tax; it assesses a 5.25% Motor Vehicle Document Fee upon titling.
Delaware permits trade-in credit deductions on both dealer and private vehicle purchases (via Form MV347).
Title fee is $35 without a lien and $55 with a lien ($35 title + $20 lien fee).
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with the Delaware DMV.
Delaware charges a 5.25% Motor Vehicle Document Fee (minimum $8.00) based on net purchase price or NADA average trade-in value.
Trade-in credit is permitted in Delaware: you may deduct the value of your trade-in vehicle from the purchase price before the 5.25% document fee is calculated.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle tax rate in Delaware?
faqs.answer: Delaware does not have a general sales tax. Instead, the Delaware DMV assesses a 5.25% Motor Vehicle Document Fee on the vehicle's purchase price or NADA average trade-in value, whichever is higher (minimum $8.00).

faqs.question: Does a trade-in reduce the vehicle document fee in Delaware?
faqs.answer: Yes! Delaware law allows you to deduct the value of your trade-in vehicle from the purchase price before calculating the 5.25% document fee. For private sales, buyers can claim this credit using Delaware DMV Form MV347 if completed within 60 days.

faqs.question: How much is a title certificate in Delaware?
faqs.answer: The Delaware DMV title certificate fee is $35.00. If the vehicle is financed with an active lien, the fee is $55.00 ($35 title + $20 lien filing fee).

faqs.question: What are registration fees in Delaware?
faqs.answer: Delaware passenger vehicle registration is $40.00 per year ($80.00 for a 2-year registration). Motorcycle registration is $15.00 per year ($30.00 for 2 years).

district-of-columbia.label: District of Columbia
notes: DC excise tax is assessed on vehicle Fair Market Value (NADA Eastern Region) at rates from 1.0% to 11.0% based on weight and EPA city MPG under the 2025 Act.
The 5.0% baseline rate models a standard passenger car (3,499 lbs or less, 21–25 city MPG).
Trade-ins on private-party sales do not reduce the DC Fair Market Value tax base.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with the DC DMV.
DC calculates vehicle excise tax based on Fair Market Value (NADA Eastern Region) and EPA city MPG tiers ranging from 1.0% to 11.0%. Baseline estimate uses standard 5.0% tier.
District of Columbia taxes full Fair Market Value — private party trade-in values do not reduce excise tax.

faqs.question: How is vehicle excise tax calculated in Washington DC?
faqs.answer: Under DC DMV regulations and the 2025 Motor Excise Tax Amendment Act, excise tax is calculated by multiplying the vehicle's Fair Market Value (NADA Eastern Region Guide) by a percentage determined by unladen weight and EPA city MPG (ranging from 1.0% to 11.0%). Standard passenger vehicles generally fall into the 3.1% to 6.0% range (5.0% average baseline).

faqs.question: Does a trade-in reduce vehicle excise tax in DC?
faqs.answer: No. In the District of Columbia, excise tax is applied to the vehicle's Fair Market Value; private party trade-in values on a bill of sale do not reduce the assessed tax base.

faqs.question: How much is a title certificate in the District of Columbia?
faqs.answer: The DC DMV certificate of title fee is $26.00 (scheduled to increase to $30.00 in 2026). If the vehicle is financed, a $20.00 lien recordation fee applies.

faqs.question: How much are vehicle registration fees in DC?
faqs.answer: DC vehicle registration is weight-based: Class I (3,499 lbs or less) is $72.00 per year ($144.00 for 2 years); Class II (3,500 lbs and over) is $115.00 per year ($230.00 for 2 years). Motorcycle registration is $52.00 per year ($104.00 for 2 years).

california.label: California
california.localTaxNote: District and county sales taxes add 0.10% to 3.00%, bringing total effective sales tax to between 7.75% and 10.75% depending on city and county.
notes: California base statewide sales and use tax rate is 7.25% (CDTFA).
Title transfer fee is $29.00; standard annual vehicle registration includes $74 base fee and $32 California Highway Patrol (CHP) fee.
Trade-in deduction is not permitted on private-party vehicle sales per Cal. Rev. & Tax. Code § 6011.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with the California DMV or CDTFA.
California use tax is assessed on the purchase price and paid directly to the DMV upon transfer of title.
Private party trade-in deductions are not permitted in California; use tax applies to the full purchase price.
Local district taxes (0.10% to 3.00%) vary by city/county and are added to the 7.25% statewide base.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate on a private car purchase in California?
faqs.answer: The California statewide base sales and use tax rate is 7.25%. Depending on your city and county of residence, local district taxes add between 0.10% and 3.00%, resulting in total effective tax rates between 7.75% and 10.75%.

faqs.question: How much does a title transfer cost in California?
faqs.answer: The standard California DMV certificate of title transfer fee is $29.00. Lien recordation is included in the standard title application.

faqs.question: Does a trade-in reduce vehicle sales tax in California private sales?
faqs.answer: No. Under California Revenue and Taxation Code Section 6011, trade-in allowances are only recognized when purchasing from licensed retail vehicle dealers. Private-party vehicle sales are taxed on the full purchase price.

faqs.question: How are California vehicle registration fees calculated?
faqs.answer: California annual registration includes a $74.00 base vehicle registration fee, a $32.00 California Highway Patrol (CHP) fee, plus county transportation fees and an annual Road Improvement Fee ($118.00) for zero-emission vehicles.

texas.label: Texas
texas.bookValueRule: Texas assesses 6.25% tax on the greater of sales price or 80% Standard Presumptive Value (SPV).
texas.localTaxNote: Texas charges a flat 6.25% motor vehicle sales tax statewide; local city and county sales taxes do not apply to motor vehicles.
notes: Texas assesses a flat 6.25% Motor Vehicle Sales and Use Tax statewide with no local sales surtaxes on motor vehicles.
Private-party sales are taxed on the higher of the purchase price or Standard Presumptive Value (SPV).
Trade-in allowance does not apply to private-party sales per Texas Comptroller Rule 3.70; trade-in deductions are restricted to licensed dealer purchases.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Texas Comptroller or TxDMV.
Texas assesses 6.25% Motor Vehicle Sales Tax on the higher of the purchase price or Standard Presumptive Value (SPV).
Trade-in deductions are not permitted on private-party vehicle sales in Texas; motor vehicle sales tax is calculated on the full sales price or SPV.
Annual inspection and local county road & bridge fees ($10–$20) are collected by the county tax assessor.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate in Texas for private sales?
faqs.answer: Texas imposes a 6.25% Motor Vehicle Sales and Use Tax. Unlike general retail purchases, motor vehicle sales in Texas are not subject to local city or transit sales taxes.

faqs.question: What is the Standard Presumptive Value (SPV) rule in Texas?
faqs.answer: Under Texas Tax Code Section 152.0412, private-party vehicle sales are taxed on whichever is greater: the actual purchase price or 80% of the vehicle's Standard Presumptive Value (SPV) as calculated by the Texas DMV database.

faqs.question: Can I deduct a trade-in on a private car sale in Texas?
faqs.answer: No. According to the Texas Comptroller, the trade-in allowance for motor vehicle sales tax only applies when purchasing from a licensed motor vehicle dealer. In a private-party transaction, sales tax must be paid on the full purchase price or Standard Presumptive Value (SPV).

faqs.question: How much are Texas title and registration fees?
faqs.answer: The statutory Texas application for certificate of title fee is $33.00 ($28.00 in non-attainment counties). Standard annual passenger car license plate registration is $51.75 plus local county road and bridge fees.

florida.label: Florida
florida.localTaxNote: Most Florida counties levy a discretionary sales surtax of 0.5% to 1.5% on the first $5,000 of purchase price.
notes: Florida state sales tax is 6.0% baseline.
Certificate of title fee is $75.25 for an electronic title ($77.75 for paper).
A statutory $225.00 initial registration fee applies for buyers without an existing Florida license plate to transfer.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with the Florida Department of Revenue or FLHSMV.
Florida state sales tax is 6.0%; counties may add a discretionary surtax (0.5%–1.5%) on the first $5,000.
A $225.00 statutory initial registration fee applies if the purchaser does not have an existing Florida license plate to transfer.
Trade-in deductions between private individuals are permitted when supported by title assignment and bill of sale.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate in Florida for private party sales?
faqs.answer: Florida levies a 6.0% state sales and use tax. Most Florida counties also impose a local discretionary sales surtax between 0.5% and 1.5%, which applies only to the first $5,000 of the purchase price.

faqs.question: How much is the Florida title transfer fee?
faqs.answer: The Florida title transfer fee is $75.25 for an electronic certificate of title for a vehicle previously registered in Florida ($77.25 for out-of-state vehicles). If the vehicle is financed, a $2.00 lien filing fee is added.

faqs.question: What is the Florida $225 initial registration fee?
faqs.answer: Florida imposes a one-time $225.00 initial registration fee on any motor vehicle registered in Florida for the first time by an owner who does not have a Florida license plate available to transfer.

faqs.question: Does Florida allow trade-in credit on private sales?
faqs.answer: Yes. If two private individuals exchange vehicles, sales tax is assessed only on the net difference in value, provided both transfers are properly documented on bills of sale and title certificates.

new-york.label: New York
new-york.localTaxNote: Local county and city sales taxes add between 3.00% and 4.875% (total sales tax is 8.875% in NYC and 8.00%–8.875% in most counties).
notes: New York State base sales tax is 4.0%; local sales taxes vary from 3.0% to 4.875% by county/city.
Title certificate fee is $50.00 pursuant to NY Vehicle & Traffic Law § 2125; recorded lien fee is $5.00 (Form MV-900).
Private-party trade-in deductions are not permitted in New York.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with NYS Department of Taxation and Finance or NYS DMV.
New York State levies a 4.0% state sales tax base; local county/city sales taxes (3.0%–4.875%) are collected by DMV at registration.
Private-party vehicle purchases do not qualify for trade-in allowance tax reductions in New York (tax is paid on full purchase price).
New York passenger vehicle registrations are issued for 2-year periods based on vehicle unladen weight.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate in New York State?
faqs.answer: New York State levies a 4.0% state sales tax. Local county and municipal sales taxes add between 3.0% and 4.875%, making the total sales tax rate 8.00% to 8.875% across most New York jurisdictions (8.875% in New York City).

faqs.question: How much is a title certificate in New York?
faqs.answer: The New York State DMV title certificate fee is $50.00. If the vehicle purchase is financed through a lienholder, an additional $5.00 lien filing fee (Form MV-900) is collected.

faqs.question: Does New York allow trade-in credit for private car sales?
faqs.answer: No. Under NYS Tax Law Section 1101, trade-in allowances only apply when trading a vehicle to a registered New York motor vehicle dealer. Private-party vehicle sales are taxed on the full purchase price without deduction.

faqs.question: How often do you renew vehicle registration in New York?
faqs.answer: New York State vehicle registrations for passenger cars are issued for a two-year period. Registration fees are calculated based on vehicle unladen weight (averaging $68.00 for vehicles under 3,700 lbs).

illinois.label: Illinois
illinois.localTaxNote: Illinois private-party vehicle purchases are reported on Form RUT-50 using statutory flat-tax tables (Table A by vehicle age under $15,000; Table B by purchase price bracket for $15,000 and over). Cook County and City of Chicago levy an additional $15 vehicle use tax.
notes: Private-party vehicle purchases in Illinois are subject to the Private Party Vehicle Use Tax (Form RUT-50).

Form RUT-50 uses statutory fixed tax tables: Table A assigns a flat tax by vehicle age for purchases under $15,000; Table B assigns a flat tax by purchase price bracket for sales $15,000 and above ($850 for $15,000–$19,999.99).
Title fee is $165.00; standard annual passenger car license plate tag fee is $151.00.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with the Illinois Department of Revenue or Cyberdrive Illinois.

Illinois assesses use tax on private-party vehicle purchases using Form RUT-50 statutory tax tables (Table A by vehicle age when under $15,000; Table B by purchase price bracket when $15,000 or greater).
Trade-in deductions are not permitted on private-party vehicle sales in Illinois; use tax is calculated on gross purchase price or vehicle age.
Standard passenger vehicle registration is $151.00 annually; electric vehicles pay an additional $100.00 annual EV road fee.

faqs.question: How is tax calculated on a private vehicle sale in Illinois?
faqs.answer: In Illinois, private-party vehicle sales are reported on Form RUT-50 (Private Party Vehicle Use Tax). Tax is not a flat percentage; it is determined by statutory tables. If the purchase price is under $15,000, tax is a flat fee based on vehicle age (Table A, ranging from $100 to $465). If the purchase price is $15,000 or greater, tax is a flat fee based on purchase price brackets (Table B, starting at $850 for $15,000–$19,999.99 up to $10,100 for $1,000,000+).

faqs.question: How much does a vehicle title cost in Illinois?
faqs.answer: The Illinois Secretary of State certificate of title fee is $165.00 for standard passenger vehicles. Lien filing is processed on the certificate without additional fee.

faqs.question: Can I deduct a trade-in on a private vehicle sale in Illinois?
faqs.answer: No. Illinois tax code does not allow trade-in credits on private-party sales reported on Form RUT-50; trade-in deductions are restricted to purchases from licensed retail dealers.

faqs.question: How much are license plate renewal fees in Illinois?
faqs.answer: Standard annual license plate registration in Illinois is $151.00 for passenger vehicles. All-electric vehicles pay an additional $100.00 annual surcharge in lieu of motor fuel tax.

ohio.label: Ohio
ohio.localTaxNote: Ohio counties levy permissive sales taxes ranging from 0.75% to 2.25%, making total effective sales tax 6.50% to 8.00% depending on county of residence.
notes: Ohio base statewide sales and use tax rate is 5.75%.
Title fee is $15.00; lien notation fee is $15.00 if financed.
Trade-in deduction is prohibited on private party sales per Ohio Rev. Code § 5739.01.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Ohio Department of Taxation or Ohio BMV.
Ohio assesses a 5.75% state sales and use tax base; county permissive taxes (0.75%–2.25%) are collected by the Clerk of Courts.
Trade-in allowances from private vehicle sales do not reduce taxable amount in Ohio (trade-in credit is dealer-only per R.C. 5739.01).
Annual passenger registration is $34.50 base; electric vehicles pay an additional $200.00 annual fee ($150.00 for hybrid).

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate in Ohio for private sales?
faqs.answer: Ohio levies a 5.75% statewide sales and use tax base. Counties levy permissive sales taxes between 0.75% and 2.25%, resulting in total combined tax rates between 6.50% and 8.00%.

faqs.question: How much does an Ohio vehicle title transfer cost?
faqs.answer: The Ohio certificate of title fee is $15.00 paid to the County Clerk of Courts Title Office. If the vehicle is financed, a separate $15.00 lien recordation fee applies.

faqs.question: Does Ohio allow trade-in credit on private car sales?
faqs.answer: No. Under Ohio Revised Code Section 5739.01, trade-in deductions are strictly limited to purchases of new or used vehicles from registered motor vehicle dealers. Private transactions are taxed on the full purchase price.

faqs.question: How much is passenger vehicle registration in Ohio?
faqs.answer: Standard annual passenger car registration in Ohio is $34.50 (plus any local county or township permissive license tax of up to $25.00). Electric vehicles incur an additional $200.00 annual state fee.

georgia.label: Georgia
georgia.localTaxNote: Georgia Title Ad Valorem Tax (TAVT) is a uniform 7.0% statewide tax that replaces all sales tax and annual ad valorem property taxes.
notes: Georgia Title Ad Valorem Tax (TAVT) is 7.0% (O.C.G.A. § 48-5C-1) assessed on the Georgia Department of Revenue fair market value.
Title fee is $18.00; standard annual license plate registration is $20.00.
Non-commercial Alternative Fuel Vehicle (AFV/EV) annual registration fee is $238.59.
Trade-in deduction is not allowed on private party sales.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Georgia Department of Revenue or County Tag Office.
Georgia assesses Title Ad Valorem Tax (TAVT) at 7.0% on the state assessment manual fair market value (or purchase price if higher).
Trade-in deductions are not available for private party sales in Georgia (only purchases from licensed Georgia dealers receive trade-in deductions).
Annual tag renewal in Georgia is $20.00; all-electric vehicles pay an annual alternative fuel fee ($238.59 in 2026).

faqs.question: What is the Georgia Title Ad Valorem Tax (TAVT)?
faqs.answer: Georgia's Title Ad Valorem Tax (TAVT) is a one-time 7.0% tax applied to vehicle purchases upon titling. TAVT replaced the old annual 'birthday tax' and general sales tax, applying uniformly across all Georgia counties.

faqs.question: How is the tax base determined for private sales in Georgia?
faqs.answer: For private-party sales, Georgia assesses TAVT on the state's vehicle assessment manual fair market value (based on DOR valuation tables), or on the actual purchase price if the purchase price is higher.

faqs.question: Can I deduct a trade-in on a private vehicle sale in Georgia?
faqs.answer: No. Under Georgia law (O.C.G.A. § 48-5C-1), trade-in allowances only reduce TAVT when purchasing a vehicle from a licensed Georgia motor vehicle dealer. Private sales do not receive trade-in credit.

faqs.question: How much are Georgia vehicle title and tag fees?
faqs.answer: The Georgia certificate of title fee is $18.00. Annual license plate registration is $20.00. Lien recordation is included on the standard title application.

north-carolina.label: North Carolina
north-carolina.localTaxNote: North Carolina levies a 3.0% Highway Use Tax (HUT) capped at $2,000 for standard passenger vehicles; no local sales taxes apply.
notes: North Carolina levies a 3.0% Highway Use Tax (HUT) in lieu of general sales tax, with a maximum cap of $2,000 for passenger vehicles.
Title fee is $56.00; lien recordation fee is $21.50.
Trade-in deduction is permitted if documented on bill of sale and title.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with NCDMV.
North Carolina charges a 3.0% Highway Use Tax (HUT) instead of general sales tax, with a maximum tax cap of $2,000 on passenger vehicles.
Trade-in allowance reduces the Highway Use Tax if you trade a vehicle with the private seller and record it properly on the title.
Standard passenger vehicle registration is $38.75 annually; electric vehicles pay an additional $140.00 annual EV fee.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle tax rate in North Carolina?
faqs.answer: North Carolina assesses a 3.0% Highway Use Tax (HUT) on the retail value or purchase price of motor vehicles in lieu of general state and local sales taxes. For private passenger vehicles, HUT is capped at a maximum of $2,000.

faqs.question: How much is a title certificate in North Carolina?
faqs.answer: The NCDMV certificate of title fee is $56.00. If the vehicle is financed, a $21.50 lien recording fee is also required.

faqs.question: Does North Carolina allow trade-in credit on private sales?
faqs.answer: Yes. If you trade a vehicle with the seller as partial payment, North Carolina allows the trade-in allowance to reduce the taxable price subject to Highway Use Tax, provided the trade is properly detailed on the title assignment.

faqs.question: How much does license plate registration cost in North Carolina?
faqs.answer: Annual registration for a private passenger car is $38.75. Fully electric vehicles are assessed an additional $140.00 annual fee ($70.00 for plug-in hybrids).

michigan.label: Michigan
michigan.localTaxNote: Michigan does not permit local option sales taxes; the 6.0% use tax is uniform statewide.
notes: Michigan assesses a uniform 6.0% state sales/use tax on motor vehicle transactions.
Title fee is $15.00; annual passenger registration is MSRP-based (MCL 257.801), averaging $150.00 for typical vehicles.
Trade-in deduction is not permitted on private party sales per Michigan law.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Michigan Department of Treasury or Michigan Secretary of State.
Michigan assesses 6.0% use tax on the purchase price or fair retail value (whichever is greater).
Private party vehicle transactions do not qualify for trade-in allowance tax credits in Michigan.
Michigan vehicle registration fees are based on the original manufacturer's suggested retail price (MSRP) of the vehicle.

faqs.question: What is the sales tax rate on a private vehicle purchase in Michigan?
faqs.answer: Michigan imposes a 6.0% use tax on private-party vehicle sales. The tax is collected by the Michigan Secretary of State at the time of titling. Michigan does not have local or county sales taxes.

faqs.question: How much does a title transfer cost in Michigan?
faqs.answer: The Michigan certificate of title transfer fee is $15.00. Lien filing is noted on the title application without an additional recording fee.

faqs.question: Does Michigan allow trade-in deductions on private car sales?
faqs.answer: No. Under Michigan MCL 205.92, trade-in tax credits only apply when purchasing a vehicle from a licensed motor vehicle dealership. Private sales are taxed on the full transaction price.

faqs.question: How are vehicle registration fees calculated in Michigan?
faqs.answer: In Michigan, registration fees for passenger vehicles (model year 1984 and newer) are determined by the vehicle's original manufacturer's suggested retail price (MSRP) when new, averaging approximately $140.00 to $180.00 per year.

new-jersey.label: New Jersey
new-jersey.localTaxNote: New Jersey does not permit local option sales taxes; the 6.625% sales and use tax is uniform statewide.
notes: New Jersey levies a uniform 6.625% sales and use tax on private party motor vehicle purchases.
Title fee is $60.00 for clean title ($85.00 with lien; $25 lien recording fee).
Registration is based on vehicle weight and age: $46.50/yr for vehicles older than 2 years under 3,500 lbs ($71.50 if over 3,500 lbs).
Zero Emission Vehicles (ZEVs) are subject to a $250 annual registration surcharge effective July 1, 2024.
Trade-in tax credits are restricted to licensed dealer purchases; private sales do not receive trade-in deductions.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with New Jersey Motor Vehicle Commission (MVC) and Division of Taxation.
Sales tax is paid directly to the NJ MVC at the time of titling and registration.
The NJ Division of Taxation monitors casual sales and may assess tax based on N.A.D.A. book value if purchase price is deemed below market value.
Trade-in allowances only reduce taxable value when purchasing from a licensed motor vehicle dealership.

faqs.question: What is the sales tax on a private car sale in New Jersey?
faqs.answer: New Jersey levies a 6.625% sales and use tax on private party motor vehicle transactions. The tax is paid directly to the New Jersey Motor Vehicle Commission (MVC) when the buyer applies for title and registration.

faqs.question: How much does a title transfer cost in New Jersey?
faqs.answer: The standard certificate of title fee in New Jersey is $60.00. If the vehicle has an active lien (is financed), the title fee is $85.00 ($60 title fee plus $25 lien recording fee).

faqs.question: Does New Jersey allow a trade-in tax credit for private sales?
faqs.answer: No. Under New Jersey sales tax regulations, trade-in deductions are exclusively permitted when trading in a vehicle with a registered motor vehicle dealer. Private party sales are taxed on the full agreed purchase price.

faqs.question: How does New Jersey verify private party vehicle sale prices?
faqs.answer: The New Jersey Division of Taxation audits casual motor vehicle sales. If the reported purchase price appears significantly below fair market value, the state may issue a casual sales inquiry and assess sales tax based on standard N.A.D.A. book values unless proof of condition or purchase price is provided.

washington.label: Washington
washington.localTaxNote: Washington local sales and use taxes add between 0.5% and 3.9% depending on locality. In the RTA district (King, Pierce, Snohomish counties), an additional 1.1% Regional Transit Authority motor vehicle excise tax applies.
notes: Washington levies a 6.8% base statewide motor vehicle use tax (6.5% general use tax + 0.3% additional motor vehicle tax per RCW 82.08.020 / RCW 82.12.020).
Tax is assessed on fair market value (FMV) using industry valuation guides (Price Digests) if the declared purchase price is below market value.
Title application fee is $15.00 (additional local service/filing fees may apply at county licensing offices).
Standard passenger vehicle registration is $68.25/yr ($43.25 base license fee + $25.00 weight fee).
Electric vehicles pay a $225 annual registration surcharge ($150 EV fee + $75 electrification fee).
Trade-in deduction is not permitted on private party sales per RCW 82.08.010.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Washington Department of Licensing (DOL) or Department of Revenue (DOR).
Washington assesses use tax on the fair market value determined by industry pricing guides if purchase price is below fair market value.
Private party vehicle transactions do not qualify for trade-in allowance tax credits in Washington.
Local sales/use taxes (0.5%–3.9%) and RTA regional transit excise taxes (1.1%) may apply based on registered address.

faqs.question: What is the tax rate on a private vehicle sale in Washington?
faqs.answer: Washington imposes a statewide base motor vehicle use tax of 6.8% (6.5% state use tax + 0.3% motor vehicle tax). In addition, local city and county taxes add between 0.5% and 3.9%, and residents in Sound Transit RTA areas pay an additional 1.1% motor vehicle excise tax.

faqs.question: How is vehicle value determined for use tax in Washington?
faqs.answer: Under Washington DOL and DOR rules, use tax is calculated on the vehicle's fair market value. The state references industry pricing databases (such as Price Digests). If the declared purchase price is within 20% of fair market value, the purchase price is accepted; otherwise, the valuation guide is used unless proof of condition or an appraisal is provided.

faqs.question: Can I deduct my trade-in on a private vehicle sale in Washington?
faqs.answer: No. Under RCW 82.08.010, the trade-in tax exclusion is strictly limited to transactions where a licensed vehicle dealer or broker accepts the trade-in as part of the sale. Private party sales cannot deduct the value of another vehicle.

faqs.question: How much does title and registration cost in Washington?
faqs.answer: The state certificate of title application fee is $15.00, and annual passenger vehicle registration is $68.25 ($43.25 basic license fee plus $25.00 weight fee), plus local licensing filing fees. Electric vehicles pay an additional $225 annual fee.

arizona.label: Arizona
arizona.localTaxNote: Private-party vehicle sales between individuals in Arizona are completely exempt from Arizona state sales tax (TPT). When titling, buyers pay title ($4), registration ($14.50), and the annual Vehicle License Tax (VLT) personal property tax.
notes: Casual / private party vehicle sales between individuals are 100% EXEMPT from Arizona Transaction Privilege Tax (TPT) and state sales tax under A.R.S. Title 42.
Title fee is $4.00; base registration fee is $14.50 ($8.00 registration + $5.00 plate fee + $1.50 air quality fee).
Arizona assesses an annual Vehicle License Tax (VLT) personal property tax based on vehicle MSRP and age ($2.89 per $100 of assessed value for used vehicles).
Lien filing fee is $4.00 if the vehicle is financed.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Arizona Department of Transportation (ADOT) MVD.
Private-party vehicle purchases between individuals are exempt from Arizona state sales tax (Transaction Privilege Tax).
An annual Vehicle License Tax (VLT) applies at registration, calculated on 60% of original MSRP depreciated at 16.25% per year.
Out-of-state vehicle purchases brought into Arizona may be subject to use tax if sales tax was not previously paid.

faqs.question: Do I have to pay sales tax on a private car purchase in Arizona?
faqs.answer: No. In Arizona, private-party vehicle sales between private individuals (casual sales) are completely exempt from Arizona Transaction Privilege Tax (TPT) and state sales tax. You pay $0 in state sales tax on a private transaction.

faqs.question: What fees do I pay when buying a car privately in Arizona?
faqs.answer: When titling and registering a private vehicle purchase at the Arizona MVD, you pay a $4.00 title fee, a $14.50 standard registration fee ($8 base + $5 plate + $1.50 air quality fee), and the annual Vehicle License Tax (VLT).

faqs.question: What is the Arizona Vehicle License Tax (VLT)?
faqs.answer: The Vehicle License Tax (VLT) is an annual personal property tax collected in lieu of ad valorem property taxes. It is calculated from 60% of the vehicle's original base MSRP, reduced by 16.25% for each year since first registration, and assessed at $2.89 per $100 of assessed value for used vehicles.

faqs.question: Does trade-in reduce tax in Arizona?
faqs.answer: Because private party vehicle sales in Arizona are already 100% exempt from sales tax, trade-in deductions do not apply to private sales. Dealership sales do allow trade-in credit to reduce dealer TPT.

tennessee.label: Tennessee
tennessee.localTaxNote: Tennessee counties levy local option sales taxes between 1.50% and 2.75% on the first $1,600 to $3,200 of purchase price, plus a single article state tax of 2.75% on amounts between $1,600 and $3,200. Many counties also assess a local wheel tax ($10 to $100+).
notes: Tennessee levies a 7.0% state sales/use tax on casual and private party motor vehicle sales collected by the County Clerk.
Title fee is $14.00 base state fee; lien notation fee is $11.00.
Standard annual passenger plate registration is $26.50/yr.
All-electric vehicles pay an additional $200.00 annual registration fee ($100.00 for hybrid vehicles).
Trade-in deduction is not permitted on private party sales per Tennessee Department of Revenue rules.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Tennessee Department of Revenue or your local County Clerk.
Casual and private party sales of motor vehicles in Tennessee are subject to the 7.0% state sales and use tax.
Trade-in tax credits are restricted to purchases from licensed dealers; private sales are taxed on the full purchase price.
Local option sales taxes (up to 2.75%), state single-article tax, and county wheel taxes may apply.

faqs.question: What is the sales tax rate on a private car purchase in Tennessee?
faqs.answer: Tennessee charges a 7.0% state sales and use tax on private-party vehicle transactions. Taxes and fees are collected by your local County Clerk when you apply for title and registration.

faqs.question: Does Tennessee exempt casual private car sales from sales tax?
faqs.answer: No. While Tennessee law exempts casual and isolated sales for many household goods, motor vehicles, vessels, and aircraft are explicitly excluded from the casual sale exemption and are fully taxable.

faqs.question: Can I deduct a trade-in on a private vehicle sale in Tennessee?
faqs.answer: No. Under Tennessee Department of Revenue regulations, trade-in allowances only reduce the taxable sales price when trading a vehicle directly with a licensed motor vehicle dealer. Private transactions are taxed on the full agreed price.

faqs.question: How much does a title and plate cost in Tennessee?
faqs.answer: The state certificate of title fee is $14.00, and standard passenger plate registration is $26.50. If financed, an $11.00 lien noting fee applies. Local county clerk processing fees and county wheel taxes may also apply.

massachusetts.label: Massachusetts
massachusetts.localTaxNote: Massachusetts has no local sales taxes on motor vehicles (uniform 6.25% statewide). However, your municipality will bill you an annual Motor Vehicle Excise tax at $25 per $1,000 of vehicle value based on state depreciation.
notes: Massachusetts assesses a 6.25% sales/use tax on private party motor vehicle purchases.
Tax is assessed on the higher of the actual purchase price or NADA clean trade-in book value per Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 64I.
Title fee is $75.00; standard passenger vehicle registration is $60.00 for a 2-year term ($30.00/yr equivalent).
Trade-in deduction is strictly limited to purchases from Massachusetts registered dealers (MGL ch. 64H/64I).
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Massachusetts RMV and Department of Revenue.
Massachusetts assesses sales tax on the higher of the purchase price or the NADA clean trade-in value.
Trade-in tax deductions are permitted only when purchasing from a registered Massachusetts motor vehicle dealer.
An annual local motor vehicle excise tax of $25 per $1,000 of assessed value is billed separately by your city or town.

faqs.question: What is the sales tax rate on a private car purchase in Massachusetts?
faqs.answer: Massachusetts imposes a 6.25% sales and use tax on private party motor vehicle purchases. Tax is paid through the Massachusetts Registry of Motor Vehicles (RMV) or MassTaxConnect (Form ST-6).

faqs.question: How does Massachusetts determine vehicle value for private sale tax?
faqs.answer: Under Massachusetts law, sales tax on a private (casual) sale is calculated on the higher of the actual purchase price or the vehicle's NADA clean trade-in value. Condition does not reduce the taxable book value.

faqs.question: Does Massachusetts allow a trade-in deduction on private sales?
faqs.answer: No. Under Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 64H and 64I, trade-in tax credits are only permitted when purchasing a vehicle from a Massachusetts registered motor vehicle dealer. Private sales must pay tax on the full value without trade-in credit.

faqs.question: How much are title and registration fees in Massachusetts?
faqs.answer: The Massachusetts RMV charges $75.00 for a Certificate of Title and $60.00 for a standard 2-year passenger registration plate.

indiana.label: Indiana
indiana.localTaxNote: Indiana does not levy local option sales taxes on vehicles (uniform 7.0% statewide). However, the BMV assesses an annual Motor Vehicle Excise Tax and local County/Municipal Wheel Tax based on vehicle age and class at registration.
notes: Indiana assesses a uniform 7.0% state sales/use tax on private party motor vehicle purchases collected at the BMV.
Title fee is $15.00; standard passenger registration is $36.35/yr ($21.35 registration + $15.00 Transportation Infrastructure Improvement Fee).
Electric vehicles pay an additional $242.00 annual supplemental fee ($81.00 for hybrid vehicles).
Trade-in deduction is not permitted on private party sales per Indiana DOR guidelines.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Indiana Bureau of Motor Vehicles (BMV) and Department of Revenue.
Private-party vehicle purchases in Indiana are subject to the 7.0% state sales and use tax.
Trade-in tax deductions apply exclusively to dealership purchases; private sales are taxed on the full purchase price.
Annual motor vehicle excise taxes and local wheel taxes are billed by the BMV based on vehicle class and age.

faqs.question: What is the sales tax on a private car purchase in Indiana?
faqs.answer: Indiana charges a 7.0% sales and use tax on private-party motor vehicle sales. The tax is collected by the Indiana Bureau of Motor Vehicles (BMV) when you title and register the vehicle.

faqs.question: Can I deduct a trade-in on a private vehicle sale in Indiana?
faqs.answer: No. Indiana Department of Revenue regulations allow trade-in credit only when purchasing from a licensed motor vehicle dealership. Private sales cannot deduct the value of a traded vehicle.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to title and register a car in Indiana?
faqs.answer: The Indiana BMV charges $15.00 for a certificate of title and $36.35 for standard annual passenger registration ($21.35 base registration plus a $15.00 Transportation Infrastructure Improvement Fee).

faqs.question: What additional taxes apply to vehicles in Indiana?
faqs.answer: In addition to sales tax at purchase, Indiana vehicle owners pay an annual Motor Vehicle Excise Tax and local county/municipal wheel taxes based on the vehicle's age and original MSRP when registering each year.

missouri.label: Missouri
missouri.localTaxNote: Missouri municipalities and counties levy local sales taxes averaging 3.0% to 5.5% (totaling 7.5% to 10.0%). Local sales tax is based on the buyer's home residential address, not the purchase location.
notes: Missouri levies a 4.225% state sales tax on motor vehicles, plus local city and county sales taxes.
Under RSMo § 144.025, trade-in allowances and replacement vehicle credits (selling a vehicle within 180 days before or after purchase) reduce the taxable purchase price for private party sales.
Title fee is $17.50 ($8.50 title fee + $9.00 title processing fee).
Registration is based on taxable horsepower: standard passenger cars (24–35 HP) pay $33.25/yr ($24.25 registration + $9.00 processing fee).
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Missouri Department of Revenue (DOR).
Missouri state sales tax is 4.225%; local city and county sales taxes apply based on your residential address.
Under RSMo § 144.025, you may deduct a trade-in or a vehicle sold privately within 180 days to reduce your taxable purchase price.
A late titling penalty of $25 per 30-day period (up to $200) applies if the vehicle is not titled within 30 days of purchase.

faqs.question: What is the sales tax rate on a car purchase in Missouri?
faqs.answer: Missouri charges a 4.225% state sales tax on motor vehicle purchases. In addition, local city and county sales taxes apply based on where the buyer resides, bringing total effective tax rates to between 7.5% and 10.0% in most areas.

faqs.question: Does Missouri allow trade-in credit for private car sales?
faqs.answer: Yes! Under RSMo § 144.025, Missouri permits trade-in credits on vehicle purchases. Furthermore, if you sell a vehicle privately within 180 days before or after purchasing another vehicle, you can claim a sold-vehicle tax credit and only pay sales tax on the net difference.

faqs.question: How much does titling and registration cost in Missouri?
faqs.answer: Titling a vehicle in Missouri costs $17.50 ($8.50 title fee plus $9.00 processing fee). Annual passenger registration for typical 24–35 taxable horsepower cars costs $33.25 ($24.25 plate fee plus $9.00 processing fee).

faqs.question: How long do I have to title a car in Missouri after a private purchase?
faqs.answer: You have 30 days from the purchase date to title and register your vehicle. Titling on or after day 31 incurs a $25.00 late penalty, which increases by $25 for every subsequent 30 days up to a maximum of $200.00.

wisconsin.label: Wisconsin
wisconsin.localTaxNote: Most Wisconsin counties levy a 0.5% county sales tax, bringing the effective sales tax rate to 5.5%. Milwaukee County levies an additional 0.4% county sales tax (total 5.9%) and the City of Milwaukee levies a 2.0% municipal sales tax (total 7.9%). Local wheel taxes ($10 to $40) may also apply.
notes: Wisconsin assesses a 5.0% state sales/use tax on private party motor vehicle purchases, plus county taxes (usually 0.5%).
Title fee is $214.50 for original or transferred title (WisDOT).
Standard automobile registration is $85.00/yr.
Electric vehicles pay an additional $175.00 annual registration surcharge ($75.00 for hybrid vehicles).
Trade-in deduction is not permitted on private party sales per Wisconsin Department of Revenue rules.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Wisconsin Department of Transportation (WisDOT) and Department of Revenue.
Wisconsin assesses a 5.0% state sales/use tax; most counties assess an additional 0.5% county sales tax.
Trade-in deductions are only permitted when purchasing from a licensed motor vehicle dealer; private party sales pay tax on full price.
Buyers must title and register within two business days of purchase.

faqs.question: What is the sales tax rate on a private car sale in Wisconsin?
faqs.answer: Wisconsin levies a 5.0% state sales and use tax on private-party vehicle purchases. In addition, most Wisconsin counties levy a 0.5% county sales tax, making the standard effective rate 5.5% (higher in Milwaukee County and the City of Milwaukee).

faqs.question: Why is the Wisconsin title fee so high?
faqs.answer: Under Wisconsin state law, the standard certificate of title fee for passenger vehicles is $214.50. This statutory fee is collected by the Wisconsin Department of Transportation (WisDOT) on all original titles and title transfers.

faqs.question: Can I deduct a trade-in on a private vehicle sale in Wisconsin?
faqs.answer: No. According to the Wisconsin Department of Revenue, trade-in tax credits are only allowed when trading in a vehicle as part of a transaction with a licensed retailer. Private sales do not receive a trade-in deduction.

faqs.question: How much is car registration in Wisconsin?
faqs.answer: Standard annual registration for an automobile in Wisconsin is $85.00. Electric vehicles pay an additional $175.00 annual surcharge ($75.00 for hybrids), and local municipal/county wheel taxes ($10 to $40) may apply depending on your location.

colorado.label: Colorado
colorado.localTaxNote: Colorado counties, cities, and special districts (such as RTD) levy local sales and use taxes ranging from 1.0% to over 6.0%, bringing total effective sales tax to between 4.0% and 9.5% depending on your residence. An annual Specific Ownership Tax (SOT) also applies at registration based on vehicle MSRP.
notes: Colorado assesses a 2.9% state sales/use tax base on private party motor vehicle purchases.
Title fee is $7.20 (state application fee); lien filing fee is $5.00.
Standard passenger vehicle registration averages $53.50/yr ($25.00 weight fee + $28.50 FASTER road safety fee).
Electric vehicles pay a $54.00 annual EV registration fee ($50 EV fee + $4 road safety).
Trade-in deduction is not permitted on private party sales per Colorado Department of Revenue rules.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Colorado Department of Revenue (CDOR) and your county motor vehicle office.
Colorado state sales tax is 2.9%; local county, city, and RTD taxes significantly increase total tax depending on where you register.
Trade-in tax deductions are restricted to purchases from licensed dealers; private sales are taxed on the full purchase price.
An annual Specific Ownership Tax (SOT) personal property tax applies at registration, calculated from vehicle MSRP and age.

faqs.question: What is the sales tax rate on a private car purchase in Colorado?
faqs.answer: Colorado imposes a 2.9% state sales and use tax on private party motor vehicle purchases. However, local city, county, and special district taxes (like RTD) usually add 2% to 6%, making total sales tax between 4.0% and 9.5% in most areas.

faqs.question: Can I deduct my trade-in on a private car sale in Colorado?
faqs.answer: No. Under Colorado Department of Revenue regulations, trade-in tax allowances are only permitted on purchases from licensed automobile dealers. Private party sales are taxed on the full purchase price.

faqs.question: How much does a title transfer cost in Colorado?
faqs.answer: The state certificate of title fee in Colorado is $7.20. If the vehicle is financed, an additional $5.00 lien filing fee applies. Transactions are processed by your local County Clerk & Recorder's office.

faqs.question: What is the Colorado Specific Ownership Tax (SOT)?
faqs.answer: The Specific Ownership Tax (SOT) is an annual personal property tax paid at registration in lieu of ad valorem property taxes. It is based on 85% of the vehicle's original manufacturer suggested retail price (MSRP) and depreciates annually as the vehicle ages.

minnesota.label: Minnesota
minnesota.localTaxNote: Minnesota Motor Vehicle Sales Tax (MVST) is 6.875% statewide under Minn. Stat. § 297B.02. Local option sales taxes do not apply to motor vehicles.
notes: Minnesota imposes a 6.875% Motor Vehicle Sales Tax (MVST) under Minn. Stat. § 297B.02 in lieu of general sales tax.
Total statutory titling fees are $23.50 ($8.25 base title + $2.25 technology surcharge + $12.00 filing fee + $1.00 transfer fee per Minn. Stat. § 168A.29 and § 168.33).
Trade-in deduction is not permitted on private-party sales under Minn. Stat. § 297B.01 subd. 14(b); trade-in credit is strictly restricted to licensed dealer purchases.
Vehicles 10 years or older with purchase price under $3,000 qualify for a flat $10 in-lieu tax (Minn. Stat. § 297B.025).
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Minnesota Driver and Vehicle Services (DVS) or Department of Revenue.
Minnesota Motor Vehicle Sales Tax is 6.875% of purchase price or fair market value.
Trade-in credit is not available for private party sales in Minnesota; tax is paid on the full purchase price.
Annual registration tax is based on vehicle MSRP and age, with an additional $150 annual fee for all-electric vehicles.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate on a private car purchase in Minnesota?
faqs.answer: Minnesota levies a 6.875% Motor Vehicle Sales Tax (MVST) under Minn. Stat. § 297B.02. Unlike general merchandise, motor vehicles are not subject to local city or county sales taxes in Minnesota.

faqs.question: Can I deduct my trade-in on a private car sale in Minnesota?
faqs.answer: No. Under Minnesota Statute § 297B.01 subd. 14(b), trade-in deductions are exclusively permitted when trading a vehicle to a licensed motor vehicle dealer. Private-to-private transactions are taxed on the full purchase price.

faqs.question: How much does a title transfer cost in Minnesota?
faqs.answer: Standard Minnesota certificate of title transfer fees total $23.50, including the $8.25 base title fee, $2.25 technology surcharge, $12.00 DVS filing fee, and $1.00 public safety transfer fee. If financed, a $2.00 lien recording fee is added.

faqs.question: How is Minnesota vehicle registration calculated?
faqs.answer: Minnesota annual vehicle registration tax is determined by the vehicle's original manufacturer suggested retail price (MSRP) and its age, plus a $15.50 plate fee and filing fees. All-electric vehicles pay an additional $150.00 annual surcharge.

south-carolina.label: South Carolina
south-carolina.localTaxNote: South Carolina assesses an Infrastructure Maintenance Fee (IMF) of 5.0% capped at a strict statutory maximum of $500.00 (S.C. Code § 56-3-627), replacing sales tax. County property taxes are billed separately.
notes: South Carolina replaces general vehicle sales tax with an Infrastructure Maintenance Fee (IMF) of 5.0% under S.C. Code Ann. § 56-3-627.
The IMF has a strict statutory cap of $500.00 — any purchase of $10,000 or greater pays exactly $500.00.
Trade-in allowance reduces the net purchase price before the 5% IMF is applied under S.C. Code § 56-3-627.
Title fee is $15.00; standard passenger vehicle registration is $40.00 biennial ($20.00/yr).
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV).
South Carolina IMF is 5.0% of the purchase price minus trade-in, capped at a maximum of $500.00.
Trade-in deductions are permitted for private party transactions when documented on the bill of sale and title assignment.
Annual county personal property taxes are assessed separately by your county treasurer before vehicle registration renewal.

faqs.question: What is the car tax rate in South Carolina?
faqs.answer: South Carolina does not charge general sales tax on vehicle purchases. Instead, the SCDMV levies an Infrastructure Maintenance Fee (IMF) of 5% of the purchase price, capped at a strict maximum of $500.00 pursuant to S.C. Code § 56-3-627.

faqs.question: Does South Carolina have a maximum cap on vehicle tax?
faqs.answer: Yes! South Carolina law limits the Infrastructure Maintenance Fee to a maximum of $500.00 regardless of how high the vehicle's purchase price is. Any vehicle priced at $10,000 or higher incurs the $500.00 cap.

faqs.question: Does a trade-in reduce tax on private vehicle sales in South Carolina?
faqs.answer: Yes. South Carolina law defines total purchase price as net of trade-in allowance. If your trade-in brings the net purchase price below $10,000, you pay 5% on the net amount; otherwise, the $500 maximum cap applies.

faqs.question: How much are title and registration fees in South Carolina?
faqs.answer: The SCDMV certificate of title fee is $15.00. Standard passenger registration is $40.00 for a two-year plate ($20.00/year equivalent). Electric vehicles pay an additional $120.00 biennial road fee ($60.00/year).

alabama.label: Alabama
alabama.localTaxNote: Alabama levies a 2.0% state automotive sales tax base (Ala. Code § 40-23-2(4)). Local county and city taxes typically add 1.0% to 4.0%, making total sales tax between 3.0% and 6.0%.
notes: Alabama levies a 2.0% statewide automotive sales/use tax on casual and private party vehicle sales (Ala. Code § 40-23-2(4) and § 40-23-61(c)).
Title application fee is $15.00 under Ala. Code § 32-8-6; lien recording is $15.00 if financed.
Trade-in deduction is not permitted on private-party sales under Ala. Code § 40-23-103; trade-in allowances are restricted to licensed dealer purchases.
Annual ad valorem property taxes are assessed by your county license commissioner at registration.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Alabama Department of Revenue (ALDOR) or your county licensing office.
Alabama charges a 2.0% state automotive sales tax; county and municipal taxes add 1.0%–4.0% depending on residence.
Private vehicle purchases do not qualify for trade-in allowance deductions in Alabama.
Annual ad valorem personal property tax is collected at registration based on the vehicle's market value.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate in Alabama for private sales?
faqs.answer: Alabama charges a 2.0% state automotive sales and use tax rate. County and city governments levy additional automotive taxes that typically range from 1.0% to 4.0%, making total sales tax between 3.0% and 6.0%.

faqs.question: Can I deduct a trade-in on a private vehicle purchase in Alabama?
faqs.answer: No. Under Ala. Code § 40-23-103, trade-in deductions are exclusively permitted when trading a vehicle to a licensed motor vehicle dealer. Private casual sales are taxed on the full agreed sales price.

faqs.question: How much does an Alabama vehicle title transfer cost?
faqs.answer: The statutory Alabama application fee for a certificate of title is $15.00 (plus a local county processing fee of $1.25–$1.50). Recording a security interest or lien costs an additional $15.00.

faqs.question: How much is vehicle registration in Alabama?
faqs.answer: The base annual state license plate fee for passenger cars is $23.00. Electric vehicles pay an additional $200.00 annual surcharge ($100.00 for plug-in hybrids) in lieu of gas tax.

louisiana.label: Louisiana
louisiana.localTaxNote: Louisiana state sales tax is 4.45% (La. R.S. § 47:302). Local parish and municipal sales taxes add 2.0% to 7.0%, bringing total effective sales tax to 6.45%–11.45% depending on your parish.
notes: Louisiana imposes a 4.45% state sales and use tax on private party motor vehicle transfers (La. R.S. § 47:302).
Title fee is $68.50; an $8.00 state handling fee and notary fees typically apply at the Office of Motor Vehicles (OMV).
Passenger license plates are issued for 2-year terms based on vehicle value ($20.00 minimum for 2 years = $10.00/year).
Trade-in deduction is not permitted on private casual sales under La. R.S. 47:303; dealer purchases only.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Louisiana Office of Motor Vehicles (OMV) or Department of Revenue.
Louisiana state sales tax is 4.45%; parish and city sales taxes (2.0%–7.0%) are collected at titling.
Private-party sales do not receive trade-in tax credits in Louisiana; tax is assessed on full purchase price.
Louisiana requires the bill of sale or title assignment to be notarized by an authorized notary public.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate in Louisiana for private sales?
faqs.answer: The Louisiana state sales tax rate is 4.45%. However, local parish and municipal taxes add between 2.0% and 7.0%, meaning buyers generally pay between 6.45% and 11.45% total sales tax when registering the vehicle.

faqs.question: Can I deduct my trade-in on a private car sale in Louisiana?
faqs.answer: No. Under Louisiana law (La. R.S. 47:303), trade-in credits are strictly limited to transactions conducted through licensed motor vehicle dealers. Private casual sales are taxed on the full purchase price.

faqs.question: Does Louisiana require a notarized bill of sale?
faqs.answer: Yes. Louisiana law requires that vehicle title assignments and acts of sale be signed in the presence of a notary public before the transfer can be processed by the Office of Motor Vehicles (OMV).

faqs.question: How much does a vehicle title cost in Louisiana?
faqs.answer: The standard Louisiana OMV title fee is $68.50 (plus an $8.00 handling fee). If the vehicle is financed, a $10.00 lien recordation fee applies.

kentucky.label: Kentucky
kentucky.localTaxNote: Kentucky assesses a flat 6.0% Motor Vehicle Usage Tax statewide (KRS 138.460). No local sales taxes apply to motor vehicles.
notes: Kentucky assesses a 6.0% Motor Vehicle Usage Tax (KRS 138.460) on the total consideration paid or retail value.
Title application fee is $9.00 under KRS 186A.130; lien filing fee is $22.00 under KRS 186A.190.
Trade-in deduction is permitted on private-party sales under KRS 138.450 when documented on a notarized Form TC 96-182 affidavit of total consideration.
Annual motor vehicle property taxes are assessed separately by your county clerk based on January 1 vehicle value.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Kentucky Transportation Cabinet (KYTC) or your County Clerk.
Kentucky charges a 6.0% Motor Vehicle Usage Tax statewide upon transfer of ownership.
Trade-in credit is permitted on private vehicle sales when both parties execute a notarized affidavit (Form TC 96-182).
Standard annual registration is $21.00; electric vehicles pay an additional $120.00 annual road fee ($60.00 for hybrid).

faqs.question: What is the vehicle tax rate in Kentucky?
faqs.answer: Kentucky imposes a 6.0% Motor Vehicle Usage Tax (MVUT) under KRS 138.460. Unlike general retail sales, motor vehicles in Kentucky are not subject to local city or county sales taxes.

faqs.question: Does Kentucky allow trade-in credit on private vehicle sales?
faqs.answer: Yes! Under KRS 138.450 and 138.460, trade-in allowances reduce taxable value for private transactions as long as both buyer and seller execute a notarized Affidavit of Total Consideration Given (Form TC 96-182).

faqs.question: How much are Kentucky title and lien fees?
faqs.answer: The Kentucky state certificate of title fee is $9.00. If the purchase is financed through a lender, an additional $22.00 lien filing fee is required by the County Clerk.

faqs.question: How much does vehicle registration cost in Kentucky?
faqs.answer: Standard annual passenger car registration in Kentucky is $21.00. All-electric vehicles pay an additional $120.00 annual electric vehicle fee ($60.00 for hybrids).

oregon.label: Oregon
oregon.localTaxNote: Oregon has no state or local sales tax on private party motor vehicle sales (0.0%). The 0.5% vehicle use tax applies only to dealer sales of new vehicles.
notes: Oregon has no general sales tax and charges 0.0% tax on private party vehicle sales.
Base certificate of title fee is $101.00 under ORS 803.090 for standard passenger vehicles.
Standard passenger vehicle registration is issued on a 2-year biennial term ($126.00 base for 0–19 MPG = $63.00/yr).
Certain metropolitan counties (Multnomah, Clackamas, Washington) assess local county registration fees of $30–$56/yr.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Oregon Driver and Motor Vehicle Services (DMV).
Oregon does not assess state or local sales tax on private vehicle transactions (0.0% tax).
Title and registration fees vary based on vehicle fuel efficiency rating (MPG) and county of residence.
Electric vehicles pay higher biennial registration fees or may opt into the per-mile OReGO program.

faqs.question: What is the car sales tax rate in Oregon for private sales?
faqs.answer: Oregon does not have a general sales tax, and private-party vehicle sales between individuals are 100% tax-free (0.0% sales tax). The 0.5% Vehicle Privilege Tax only applies to licensed dealers selling new vehicles.

faqs.question: How much does a title transfer cost in Oregon?
faqs.answer: Under ORS 803.090, the base Oregon DMV certificate of title fee for standard passenger cars is $101.00. Lien notation is processed on the title application without an extra filing fee.

faqs.question: How are registration fees calculated in Oregon?
faqs.answer: Oregon registers passenger vehicles on a two-year cycle with fees tiered by EPA fuel economy rating, starting at $126.00 for vehicles under 20 MPG ($63.00/year equivalent). Tri-county areas (Multnomah, Washington, Clackamas) add local county fees.

faqs.question: Do electric vehicles pay extra fees in Oregon?
faqs.answer: Yes. All-electric vehicles pay an increased biennial registration fee ($316.00 for 2 years) to compensate for untaxed motor fuel, or owners may enroll in Oregon's voluntary road usage charge program (OReGO).

oklahoma.label: Oklahoma
oklahoma.localTaxNote: Oklahoma levies a 3.25% Motor Vehicle Excise Tax on used vehicles under 68 O.S. § 2103. A 1.25% state sales tax applies to new vehicle retail sales.
notes: Oklahoma levies a 3.25% Motor Vehicle Excise Tax under 68 O.S. § 2103 on the purchase price or taxable value of used vehicles.
Title fee is $11.00 through Service Oklahoma; lien filing fee is $10.00.
Annual registration fees are age-based: $96.00 for years 1–4, $86.00 for years 5–8, $66.00 for years 9–12, and $46.00 for years 13–16.
Trade-in deduction is not permitted on private party sales under 68 O.S. § 2103.
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Service Oklahoma or an authorized licensed operator.
Oklahoma charges a 3.25% Motor Vehicle Excise Tax on the purchase price of used vehicles transferred between individuals.
Trade-in tax deductions are not available for private party vehicle sales in Oklahoma.
Annual registration tag fees decrease as the vehicle ages according to Oklahoma statutory age brackets.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle tax rate in Oklahoma for private sales?
faqs.answer: In Oklahoma, used vehicle transfers between private parties are subject to a 3.25% Motor Vehicle Excise Tax under 68 O.S. § 2103, assessed on the actual purchase price or fair market value.

faqs.question: Can I deduct my trade-in on a private vehicle sale in Oklahoma?
faqs.answer: No. Oklahoma law does not allow trade-in credit deductions on private-party vehicle transactions. Motor vehicle excise tax must be paid on the full purchase price.

faqs.question: How much does a title transfer cost in Oklahoma?
faqs.answer: The standard Service Oklahoma certificate of title fee is $11.00 (plus an optional $17.00 ownership transfer fee at licensed operators). Lien recordation costs $10.00.

faqs.question: How are vehicle registration fees calculated in Oklahoma?
faqs.answer: Oklahoma uses a flat age-based annual registration schedule: $96.00 for vehicles 1 to 4 years old, $86.00 for 5 to 8 years old, $66.00 for 9 to 12 years old, $46.00 for 13 to 16 years old, and $26.00 for 17+ years.

connecticut.label: Connecticut
connecticut.bookValueRule: Connecticut assesses 6.35% tax on the higher of the purchase price or NADA Eastern Edition average trade-in value.
connecticut.localTaxNote: Connecticut sales/use tax is 6.35% (7.75% for luxury vehicles over $50,000) under C.G.S. § 12-408. Municipal personal property taxes are assessed annually by your town.
notes: Connecticut levies a 6.35% sales and use tax (C.G.S. § 12-408) on private casual vehicle sales (7.75% luxury rate for vehicles over $50,000).
Tax is assessed on the higher of the bill of sale purchase price or NADA Eastern Edition average trade-in book value.
Title fee is $25.00 under C.G.S. § 14-192; lien filing fee is $10.00.
Trade-in deduction is not permitted on private-party sales under C.G.S. § 12-408; dealer sales only.
Base passenger registration is $120.00 for a 3-year term ($40.00/yr equivalent).
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Connecticut Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) or DRS.
Connecticut sales tax is 6.35% on the higher of purchase price or NADA book value (7.75% on vehicles over $50,000).
Trade-in allowances from private vehicle sales cannot be deducted from taxable purchase price in Connecticut.
Municipal property tax on motor vehicles is billed separately each year by your local city or town tax collector.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate in Connecticut for private sales?
faqs.answer: Connecticut charges a standard 6.35% sales and use tax on private party motor vehicle purchases. If the vehicle purchase price or book value exceeds $50,000, a luxury tax rate of 7.75% applies instead.

faqs.question: How is the tax base determined for private sales in Connecticut?
faqs.answer: Under Connecticut DMV regulations, use tax is calculated on either the purchase price stated on the bill of sale or the NADA Official Used Car Guide (Eastern Edition) average trade-in value, whichever is higher.

faqs.question: Can I deduct my trade-in on a private vehicle sale in Connecticut?
faqs.answer: No. Under Connecticut General Statutes § 12-408, trade-in credits are strictly restricted to transactions with licensed motor vehicle dealers. Private casual sales are taxed on the full purchase price or book value.

faqs.question: How much are Connecticut vehicle title and registration fees?
faqs.answer: The Connecticut DMV title certificate fee is $25.00. Standard passenger registration is $120.00 for a three-year cycle ($40.00/year equivalent), plus mandatory state Clean Air and Passport to the Parks fees.

utah.label: Utah
utah.localTaxNote: Utah state sales tax base is 4.85% (Utah Code § 59-12-103). Local county, city, and transit taxes add 1.25% to 4.20%, making total combined sales tax between 6.10% and 9.05% depending on your residence.
notes: Utah imposes a 4.85% state sales and use tax base on private party motor vehicle sales under Utah Code § 59-12-103.
Title fee is $6.00 under Utah Code § 41-1a-1201; lien notation is included on the standard title application.
Base passenger vehicle registration is $44.00 under Utah Code § 41-1a-1206, plus an age-based statewide uniform fee ($10–$150).
Trade-in deduction is not permitted on private-party sales under Utah Code § 59-12-102; dealer purchases only.
Electric vehicles pay an additional $138.50 annual road usage fee ($56.50 for plug-in hybrids).
disclaimers: Estimates only — not tax or legal advice. Verify with Utah State Tax Commission and Utah DMV.
Utah charges 4.85% state sales tax; local county and transit taxes increase the total rate to between 6.10% and 9.05%.
Trade-in deductions are not available for private party vehicle sales in Utah.
An age-based uniform fee ($10.00 to $150.00) is collected at registration in lieu of personal property tax.

faqs.question: What is the vehicle sales tax rate in Utah for private sales?
faqs.answer: Utah levies a 4.85% state sales tax on motor vehicles. Combined with local city, county, and transit taxes, total effective tax rates range from 6.10% to 9.05% depending on the buyer's home address where the vehicle is registered.

faqs.question: Can I deduct my trade-in on a private vehicle sale in Utah?
faqs.answer: No. Under Utah Code § 59-12-102, trade-in allowances only reduce sales tax when trading a vehicle to a licensed motor vehicle dealer. Private sales are taxed on the full purchase price.

faqs.question: How much does a vehicle title cost in Utah?
faqs.answer: The Utah DMV certificate of title fee is $6.00. Lien recordation is included directly on the standard title application without extra fees.

faqs.question: What is the Utah age-based vehicle fee?
faqs.answer: Utah charges an annual age-based uniform fee at registration in place of ad valorem property taxes. The fee scales from $150.00 for vehicles less than 3 years old down to $10.00 for vehicles 12 or more years old, added to the $44.00 base registration fee.
